sections.h2: Quickest ways to sell in Titusville
sections.html:
Cash from an investor is normally the fastest route. A listing priced to move comes second, and a sale to someone you know is a third option. Repairs, title and your payoff balance decide which one fits.

Titusville sits along the Indian River in Brevard County, and its housing grew up around Kennedy Space Center. In the boom decades after the 1950s, motels, subdivisions and shopping centers arrived, so plenty of houses here are old enough that an inspector heads straight for the roof, plumbing and wiring. Price with that in mind, or pick a buyer who takes the house as it stands.

  • Investor purchase: no lender appraisal, and you name the closing day.
  • Listing: a bigger pool of buyers, with more prep and more waiting.
  • As-is deal: no repair bills for you, at some cost in price.

Before inviting offers, find your deed, the newest tax bill and a payoff letter from your lender, if you have a mortgage. That packet lets each buyer judge the house on the same facts.

The city rests on a dune ridge above the Indian River Lagoon, with Merritt Island and Cape Canaveral to the east and wetlands of the St. Johns River watershed to the west. Water, drainage and flood questions therefore come up in many sales.

Spanish Revival houses from the 1920s land boom and older riverfront homes still stand around town. If you own one, say so. Character and age cut both ways: some buyers pay extra for it, and others subtract the repairs. Regular rocket launches have also made the city a draw for space workers, and a buyer relocating for a job at the Cape often wants a short closing. That is one reason a seller with clean title can ask for speed.

  • Ask the Brevard County Property Appraiser for your parcel's flood zone before you list.
  • Keep elevation certificates, roof records and permits together for buyers.
  • Expect insurance questions on older construction near water.

sections.h2: Papers to gather for an older house
sections.html:
A buyer who sees dated records trusts the house more, and an investor can price repairs without guessing. Photograph period details such as stucco, tile roofing or original millwork, since a buyer who wants character will notice them.

  • List the year of the roof, panel and plumbing, if you know them.
  • Keep any termite or moisture reports in one folder.
  • Note any additions built without a permit, and ask the building department how to close them out.
  • Ask planning staff which zoning district covers your lot.

Call the building department to learn whether your address has open permits or code cases, because an unresolved item can stall a closing at the last minute. On a big lot, an investor may wonder about other uses, and the city is the one to answer that. For guest rentals, check the city's current code before telling anyone the house can run as a vacation rental.

Deed tax is the main charge. Brevard pays the standard statewide rate of seventy cents per hundred dollars of price, not Miami-Dade's separate scheme. A mortgage that stays on the property still counts as part of the price.

Deed charges on a Brevard County sale
ChargeRule
Deed tax rate70 cents per $100, all counties but Miami-Dade
Who is liableAll parties to the document
Collected byThe clerk, at recording
Clerk page fees$5.00 first page, $4.00 each added page, plus add-ons

The title agent works out exact totals before closing. Request them early, while you can still weigh an offer against them.

sections.h2: Your Brevard property tax after the sale
sections.html:
In Brevard, value is fixed each January 1 and bills go out in November. Your homestead exemption is worth up to $50,000, and the capped value can only grow so much while you keep it.

The sale ends that protection, and the buyer starts at full just value the following January 1, so their bill may run well above yours. Buying again in Florida? The Brevard County Property Appraiser can explain how part of your cap moves to the new house. Set up the new homestead within three years, and file by March 1.

Every one of these has a deadline. Courts schedule a foreclosure sale 20 to 35 days after judgment, with a 5 percent deposit from the top bid. A short probate path exists for estates of $150,000 or less, or when the owner died over two years ago.

Unpaid property tax turns delinquent on April 1. Certificates go up for sale by June 1, and two years later a buyer can apply for a tax deed. Homestead property opens at half its last assessed value plus the amount owed. Because those results are hard to undo, speak with a Florida attorney or title company before acting.

sections.h2: How a quick sale works step by step
sections.html:
A fast sale follows the same few steps whoever the buyer is, and knowing them helps you set a realistic date.

  1. Gather your paperwork.
  2. Take an offer and ask whether the buyer wants an inspection first.
  3. A title company opens the file and looks for liens, back taxes and open permits.
  4. You read the settlement statement and sign the deed at closing.
  5. The clerk records the deed and takes the deed tax.

A cash buyer brings no lender review, so timing hinges mostly on how clean the title is. Owe back taxes? The title company can ask the Brevard tax collector for a payoff and pay it out of your proceeds at closing.

A cash buyer does not need a mortgage approval, so the deal avoids the lender's appraisal and the repair demands that sometimes follow it. You also skip staging, open houses and the weeks of waiting between a showing and a contract.

The trade is price. An investor builds repair costs and risk into the offer, so expect a figure under what a polished retail listing might reach. Compare the two honestly, counting the mortgage payments, insurance and tax bills you carry during a longer sale.

Read every offer for who pays which closing charges, whether the buyer may walk away after an inspection, and when you hand over keys. Ask a Florida attorney or title company to look at the contract if anything is unclear. Never sign a deed until you have seen the settlement statement and know what lands in your account.

If anyone is living in the house, sort out the move-out date in writing. If a relative co-owns the property or an estate is still open, every owner or the personal representative has to be ready to sign, or the closing will slip.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Titusville house without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. An as-is buyer accepts the condition and prices it in. Ask a Florida attorney or title company what you must disclose about known defects.

faqs.q: How much is the state deed tax here?
faqs.a: It is seventy cents on each hundred dollars of price, because Brevard is not Miami-Dade. Everyone on the deed is liable, and the clerk collects at recording.

faqs.q: Which office keeps Titusville land records?
faqs.a: The Brevard County clerk of the circuit court records deeds and other land documents for the city.

faqs.q: Will the buyer owe the same property tax I do?
faqs.a: Probably not. A change of ownership resets value on the next January 1, and your homestead does not pass to the buyer.

faqs.q: I owe back taxes. Can I still sell?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask the title company for a payoff figure from the Brevard tax collector, and tell it right away about any tax certificate on the house.
